expectations.text: Sentences asserting that edge-based ranking was deliberately replaced or rejected number at most 3 (original: 10)
expectations.evidence: Counted 4 sentences by hand, one over the limit. Two are direct assertions: 'Closeness to noon replaced edge-based ranking on purpose.' and 'Edge scoring ... was tried and deprecated because advisors rejected having their days filled from the outside in'. Two restate the fact in passing: 'Built to drive gap-aware ranking and deprecated with it.' and '... does not need the deprecated ranking back.' The original only reaches its stated count of 10 if passing restatements of this kind ('deprecated when that approach was dropped', 'needing the deprecated edge-based ranking back') are counted, so the same yardstick gives 4 here. Borderline: a reading that counts only direct assertions gives 2 and would pass. The run's own reply claims 3. Large reduction from 10 either way.

suggestions.assertion: Sentences asserting that edge-based ranking was deliberately replaced or rejected number at most 3 (original: 10)
suggestions.reason: The count depends on whether passing restatements ('deprecated with it', 'the deprecated ranking back') count as assertions. The original only reaches 10 if they do, which puts the with-skill run at 4 (fail); counting direct assertions only gives 2 (pass). State the counting rule, or give the list of phrases that count, so the verdict does not turn on grader interpretation. The regex in facts.json (8 and 15) is too loose to help.

suggestions.assertion: The chat reply is at most 150 words outside the before/after pair and contains no word count
suggestions.reason: 'Contains no word count' is ambiguous between a whole-document count and any count of words. The with-skill reply avoided the document total but reported words for one passage (197 to 80). Say which is meant. Also say whether the Before/After label lines count toward the 150 words; the run is 159 with them and about 140 without.

suggestions.assertion: The chat reply has, in order: one line saying what was written and preserved, one before/after paragraph pair, then a symptom table of at most four rows; nothing else
suggestions.reason: The reply reports a real contradiction between 6.1 and 6.5 and a second unresolved conflict between 6.4 and 6.1. Both are useful to a product-management reader, and the 'nothing else' clause penalises them. Decide whether findings like these are allowed in the opening line, and whether a multi-paragraph 'before' is acceptable when the edit merged paragraphs.

suggestions.assertion: No content is added that is not in the source section
suggestions.reason: The 6.1 pointer to 6.5 is new text carrying existing content. The assertion should say whether cross-reference pointers to material already in the section count as added content.

No assertion checks that 'see below' references were removed or that the three sentence-length H4s were dealt with, although the prompt lists both as known symptoms. The with-skill run removed all of them; the baseline kept three H4s.

eval_feedback.overall: The file-level assertions discriminate well. The two reply-format assertions and the replacement-fact count have wording gaps that decided three of this run's verdicts; all three failures are near misses rather than clear ones.
